utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify your position, I'm going to put a certain number of questions to you. These will be quite simple questions that you will easily be able to answer with "yes" or "no" in order to cut short your testimony as much as possible. The attendees of the training centre, were they employed by the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. They didn't receive insignia, they did not sign any papers or anything like that, for as long as I was there, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony yesterday, you told us, in a lot of details, speaking about your professional career and the training you went through, you told us in detail about the training courses that you completed. According to your best recollection, did any of the attendees that you worked with in Jahorina have any police training course completed from the ones that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You practically anticipated some of my questions, but did you ever see any of those participants in the training of the Jahorina Centre receive orders on the schedule or any paperwork indicating that they had been employed full time by the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they receive salaries during that time from the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the attendees of the Jahorina Centre, were they authorised to wear insignia of the Special Police Brigade which you would recognise when the Prosecutor showed you footage of Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade insignia is received by the detachment members and members of the -- or the command brigade. They were not in either one. They were in no way members of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just something more on that topic. It's about the candidate admission procedure into the ranks of the Special Police. The candidate who would like to join the Special Police Brigade would need to complete a certain type of training; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this training comprised the policemen course, and the candidate also had to have completed high school, at least, or secondary school, at least?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He also had to pass physical and mental fitness testing?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the usual procedure for all employees seeking jobs at the MUP, and there was some additional testing in case of admission to the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Only after all these conditions were met would a contract be signed on employment with the RS MUP with a particular person?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And after being accepted, the person would receive an identification card and be deployed into one of the detachments you mentioned. They would receive the insignia of the brigade with a number, which would be their ID number within the brigade; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to specifically talk about the uniforms that the members of the Jahorina Centre wore. They didn't have overalls that members of the special unit wore; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And according to the statement you gave to the Prosecution, their uniforms were actually different versions of camouflage uniforms, and what made them -- identified them were the belts and the boots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also, speaking about the uniforms, you said in your statement to the Prosecution that before leaving for Bratunac, the members received a certain amount of flak jackets. These were camouflaged flak jackets of the RS Army. When we looked at this footage now shown to you by the Prosecutor and when you saw this person, Miki, in a short blue flak jacket, does that help you to remember? And there was some testimony to this effect, that a number of these short-blue flak jackets were also distributed shortly before leaving for Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as these flak jackets or this protection equipment, there was a shortage of that kind of thing even in the Special Unit, so I was surprised that this was distributed in the training centre because no combat assignments were expected, so why the flak jackets? I think that some foreign organisation brought these flak jackets to the brigade as some form of sample, something that we could possibly order or not, and since they were not particularly suited to our use and were not of an acceptable protection level, some of them sort of were left behind. But it's possible. I didn't personally distribute these, so it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you have given us very important information in this regard. But when you were in Potocari and when you saw a UN observer, I'm not talking about the DutchBat, I'm talking about the observers who wore long, bulletproof vests that protected also the neck, not only the upper part of the body, those were not the same vests that we saw on Miki?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I didn't pay attention. If you have some more photographs or video footage, I could tell you more because I am quite well-versed in protection equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That won't be necessary. I would only like to ask you a couple more questions concerning the brigade of the Special Police again, but in broader terms, the police force of Republika Srpska in July of 1995, you have mentioned the subject in your interview with the investigators, but since it hasn't been the subject of your testimony before, I would like to go through it briefly. In July 1995, members of the police of Republika Srpska did not have ranks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the time, as you have said before in your statement on page 9, there were only functional distinctions?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And to clarify it to the Trial Chamber, this difference between ranks and functional distinctions, I would like to show you an exhibit, 4D103. It's an instruction of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska in 1992, designating the functional distinctions of MUP members. Unfortunately, the document is not in e-court. We received it from our investigator very recently, and I would like us just to have a look at it. It's a booklet, and the last page indicates the designations of various functions within the police force. Could we put it on the ELMO? [In English] Your Honours, I already gave this evidence to my colleagues from the Prosecution, and I have some additional hard copies. As soon as it comes on e-court system, I will submit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djuric, please have a look at it. You see on the screen, the marks of various functions within the police from 1992 until November 1995, according to our information. Can you confirm that this is, in fact, what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the functional designations, distinctions, of various members of the police. The categorisation, of course, is consistent with job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I would now like briefly to have a look at a still taken from a video, if we can move to e-court. It's a video we received, V00-6846. We received it from the Prosecution. And the counter starts at 1715 and lasts until 1725.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We don't need to hear the sound. It's just to show the witness the functional insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I am also allowed to ask you leading questions, unlike the Prosecutor. We see Ljubomir Borovcanin in this picture; right?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And what he's wearing on his shoulders are the marks of his function within the police?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at another functional insignia on the ELMO? You will agree that it's, in the middle line, the second one from the bottom? Sorry, from the top.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it is called Assistant Detachment Commander?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we zoom in? Is there any way we can zoom in that -- we would still need to focus. Do you wish to stipulate, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can. I just want to clarify something for the record, though, that I think may cure some of the confusion. I think the transcript says, "Second from the top," but I'm not sure that's correct. I think that may be the source of the problem we're having.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My colleague is 100 per cent right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992, just to clear this up, the Brigade of the Special Police did not exist, only the detachment existed, so it's practically the same thing, only in 1995 it was the brigade level; correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we are talking about the central column, the second insignia from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the same column now, but the first insignia on top with three stars and one short line. Is that the one you wore in the special brigade, Police Inspector First Class?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had the second one from the top in the central column.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry about this. Maybe I misidentified your functional insignia.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can clear up one thing, since you mentioned it. From 1992 until 1995, the Special Brigade kept changing. It started with a company, then several companies, then detachment, then several detachments. Such things were not decided for one unit only. They were decided and determined centrally for the force. So I don't think it's really correct that these things changed from month to month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But what I want to know specifically is this: In July 1995, Ljubomir Borovcanin could not have had the rank of lieutenant-colonel because that rank did not exist within the police force at all?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Ranks were introduced in November 1995 in the police of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I remember it was in '95.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next thing I would like to show you on the screen is Defence exhibit 4D98, and it depicts ranks on the police force of the Republika Srpska when they were introduced. Will you please take a look. Can you just confirm that that's what rank insignia looked like in the police force of Republika Srpska once they were introduced?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. That's it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the first rank in the police that you received?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major, police major.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So practically you have never been a captain of the police; you were a major from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And if, in July of 1995, somebody designated you as Captain Mane, that person would have been wrong; right?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, because ranks did not exist then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When I was showing you these insignia, and it's my mistake, the document is on two pages and I just showed you the first one. In order to be able to tender this exhibit, could you please look at the second page as well? Can you just confirm, since this is page 2, that these two are rank insignia once they were introduced late in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will move on to another subject now, to discuss the events of the 11th, 12th, 13th and 14th. To take it chronologically from the moment you and your unit set out from Jahorina to Bratunac, we have heard testimony before this Tribunal that before the company set out on the 11th of July, the then-commander of the brigade addressed the men from Jahorina, warned them of the seriousness of the task that is awaiting them. Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But during those days, let us focus on the 10th and 11th of July, 1995, you did not see Ljubomir Borovcanin at the Jahorina Centre at all?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before setting out towards Bratunac, the members of your unit did not have time to complete their training; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you set out, together with them, on the road to Bratunac. Could you tell me, what was the prevailing sentiment among the members of the unit concerning what was awaiting them? How did they feel before they left for Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before leaving for Bratunac, we had a drill, a drill that had to do with guarding a road. It was our joint exercise. And when we received orders to go to Bratunac, we were told that this was going to be police work. We didn't know exactly what we were going to do. And the term "police work" was not exactly clear to them, and they had a lot of questions, what it was going to be like and what it's going to involve, and the evening before they asked me many questions. They were not policemen, and everything that had to do with police work was foreign to them. It must have sounded odd.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So practically, when you were leaving, you and the members of your unit did not know what your task was going to be there?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we just knew it was going to be police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then on the 11th of July, you arrived at Bratunac. Can you tell us more about it? Of course, I don't expect you to tell us the exact time, but was it in the morning, noon, afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday in your testimony, responding to one of the Prosecutor's questions, you said that a total of around 70 members from the training centre arrived at Bratunac. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the number 70, that's less than the full complement of one company?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "70", and a full company should be many more. One part of them left with me, but the unit had never been fully reinforced, according to establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that same evening, then, when that, let's say, reduced company arrived, two men had already run away?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two of them escaped before we reached our destination. In fact, they had asked for my permission to go and visit their families, but they never -- they never returned. They simply cheated me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And apart from those two who ran away --

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another 10 or so escaped. The base where we were located was next to the Drina River, and Serbia is on the other side. They had ample opportunity to leave; the proximity of the river made it only easier. That's what I suppose. I did not investigate, but I suppose they crossed the river and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. So that evening on the 11th of July, you received an assignment from Dusko Jevic for the next day. I'd like us to discuss that, with an eye on the statement you gave to the investigators. It's going to be roughly the same subject as you discussed with the Prosecutor. You were told that close to the UN base it was expected that a large number of civilians would gather, that you were to secure that area, and that representatives of the authorities were going to negotiate about what is to be done with those civilians, whether they were going to be moved to Tuzla or something else; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we were told, the assignment we were given.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You didn't receive any kind of written order from Dusko Jevic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, throughout my whole stay I did not receive any written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we were to break down this answer that you gave into certain segments to see what they are telling us, let's do that. From the order, we can find out that Muslims were already gathering in Potocari, that they had fled Srebrenica, and that it was expected that an even greater number of them would come to the UNPROFOR base; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so. Since we were engaged to secure them, it can be assumed that a larger group were expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So on the 11th, in the evening, already people were arriving to Potocari, and they expected even more people? I'm asking this because of the time that was established for this. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The assignment given to you was practically to prevent unrest from breaking out in the crowd, preventing attacks or harassment of them by members of different units, or even revengeful civilians; would that be a fair description of your assignment?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assignment was not put in writing. It wasn't a classic assignment, so it was stated freely. And this first remark about unrest breaking out amongst the civilians, I don't recall that, but everything else stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to insist on something that --

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that particular item.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is important about the timing is that on the 11th, in the evening, when you received the assignment, practically it is still unclear what will happen with the civilians, it's not known and you cannot know it. You had information that negotiations were underway and that politicians or the authorities, whoever, will find a solution about what to do with the civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can recall, I think that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you received your assignment from Jevic, were you told that members of your unit should attack the UNPROFOR observation post at Zuti Most or to attack the United Nations base at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In view of what we talked about just a while ago about the composition of your unit and so on, would that have been possible with a unit such as yours, to carry out an attack on the UNPROFOR base or the observation post?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With that group of people, I would not embark on any kind of attack, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After this order, you already told us that you talked with members of the unit about what will happen "tomorrow." Did you try to calm them down? Were they frightened, upset?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, in the morning, you set off, as you said, from Bratunac towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until that check-point that was at some point the line of separation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is if the whole unit set off that day or did some members remain at the school?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a reserve group that stayed with the equipment and the things that were there, because we just took our personal belongings with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of those 70-odd people, as you said, how many left with you? Or to rephrase it, how many stayed at the school where you were billeted?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't give you the numbers, because I don't remember. Perhaps about 40, 45 people were with me, let's say that, but I really cannot recall the numbers. Forgive me, but it's been a long time since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to insist on the exact number. I just wanted to get an approximate picture of how it was at the departure and what were the numbers that you entered the protected zone with. When you passed Zuti Most, as it's called here, you talked today about how there was a UN observation post on the right side, and we called that observation post OP Papa here, so I would like to put some questions to you about that. When you passed along the road, it was on the right-hand side, and there were Dutch soldiers there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that detail at all. I know that there was some observation post we passed by. I have no memory of if there were any people there, or how many. Please believe me when I say that I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But let's put this question a little differently now. You and members of your unit did not open fire at the Papa OP when you entered the zone?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And they didn't open fire at you?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Had something like that happened, you would have remembered it, surely?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had we opened fire or had fire been opened at us, I would definitely have remembered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The evening before, when you were with Dusko Jevic, you said that he had informed you that the Army of Republika Srpska had already passed that way and that no danger was expected for your unit. However, did he tell you that there were still certain groups that he didn't know where, and that it was possible that some danger would be coming from some Muslim groups?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although he was aware of the kind of unit that we were, he told me that there were no obstacles, that there were no formations that we would have to go into conflict with, that the Army of Republika Srpska had passed by there, that the terrain was clear, and that we needed to be careful in any case because maybe some group could have been infiltrated during the night or something like that. And that is why I deployed my men in a semi-combat position, and that is how we were moving, just in case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And in the time from the observation post as you were going towards the UN base, did you hear firing from surrounding hills?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they warned me that these houses were burning. As for the shooting, as far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you talked about the vehicles arriving at Potocari, that at one point they arrived and that the evacuation started, evacuation of the population, you described in detail the job that you were doing. You already said here that you saw members of some other military formations that were escorting the transports that were present on the 12th and the 13th in Potocari. Did you perhaps notice something characteristic about them, some insignia markings, so that you would be able to tell us to which units the soldiers belonged?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During that time in Potocari, the 12th and the 13th, the Dutch practically carried out the same jobs as you did?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less the same. I wasn't checking on what they were doing, but we were there together that whole time, so I assume that their assignments were the same as ours or similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us now to look at a short clip from the video footage tendered by the Prosecution. It's a clip from a meeting at the Fontana Hotel on the 12th of July, 1995, where the evacuation of the civilian population was agreed. This is Exhibit P20 -- it's Exhibit P2047. The number of the video is V000-4458, and the counter starts at 0.150.42, and it goes on to 0.59.09.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You will see it soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to assist you a little, I would like to see first if you understood what these gentlemen are saying in the footage.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, the gentleman from the UN, the UN officer, said that he received an assignment from his ministry to assist in the evacuation, if I understood that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, precisely that. My question is: No, now that you've seen this, is whether the Dutch acted in accordance with their orders. Did they act in accordance with the orders of their commander and he, in turn, did he act upon the instructions from his defence ministry, as stated here?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little unclear to me, what I should state.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question. We've seen in this footage Colonel Karremans, the commander of DutchBat at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you heard in the footage that said that he received an assignment from his - the Dutch - Ministry to assist in the evacuation of civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that he was offering the help of his battalion in the action. When you came to Potocari and you contacted the Dutch throughout that whole day and the next day that you described, is that what the Dutch actually did, is that what Lieutenant Karremans promised to do to Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can count the part of assisting civilians as assistance in the evacuation, then that would be that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is what I wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organising transport was mentioned here as well, so I was a little bit unclear. That's why I wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In order to clarify your answer, I would like to know if you had any duties in relation to the transport itself.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that makes your answer quite clear. On the 12th of July, 1995, this is this first day in Potocari, you personally did not see mistreatment, violence, unlawful conduct of the members of your unit towards members of the local civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, also you did not have contacts with Ljubomir Borovcanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you did not see him at all on the 12th in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since my question was put in a negative form and in order to understand the response properly, I asked you: "You did not have contacts with Ljubomir Borovcanin; is that correct?" And you said, "No." So we don't want it to be understood that you did have contact.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any contacts with Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now it's clear. Just one more question, because I can see that we're coming quite close to the break. On the 12th, you didn't have radio communications with Ljubomir Borovcanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had no contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The only contact by radio was the one you had with Dusko Jevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's convenient for you, yes. Let's have a break, 25 minutes, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djuric, to continue with the cross-examination, if you recall we stopped at the question that had to do with your radio communications being only with Dusko Jevic, and you replied that that was so. Now I would just like to continue on from there. Did Dusko Jevic ever, on the 11th, the 12th, or the 13th of July, tell you that you needed to separate able-bodied Muslim men in Potocari from the rest of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did any members of your unit take part in these activities amongst the men gathered in Potocari? We know that there were many of them, but out of that large number, were they meant to be separated from the other civilians, men who were from 16 to 60?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that, and I can guarantee that where I was, this is something that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Another question about this. The Prosecutor asked you something similar, but did you or your unit ever receive orders from Dusko Jevic, or anyone else, to take the weapons from members of the DutchBat, their bulletproof vests, their radios, or any other equipment?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the screen. It's part of a video that has already been used here, P2047. I have already shown to you another part of it, and what I want to see together with you is at 02.26.04.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we could play this once again to see it better. Could you please pay attention to what you're holding in your hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is he holding in his hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm holding in my hand is a Motorola, a hand-held radio, my Motorola that I had used for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And to clear this up completely, it's certainly not a held-hand radio that had belonged to any DutchBat members?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not. All senior members of our unit held hand-held radios they had been issued from supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with that radio we've just seen, were you able to get in touch with members of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's technically possible, but I don't know. I wasn't in touch with any DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You explained to us in detail what you did in Potocari on the 12th of July, and I would just like to clear up one more thing. The job that you were doing is not what the company from Sekovici or the PJP were doing; they were not working with you?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question was not fully recorded. I said the 1st Company of the PJP, of the Public Security Centre, Zvornik. And the 2nd Detachment of the Special Police Brigade from Sekovici. I suppose I don't need to repeat the question. You understood me. I just did this for the record. Thank you very much. Can you tell me, what was approximately the time when, on the 12th, you left Potocari with your unit?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact time, but it was late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from your unit perhaps stay in Potocari after the unit departed?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of my members stayed in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps whether during the night of the 12th any members of your unit came to Potocari and came close to Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, our assignment was to cover the road, to guard the road, and in between that we were at the base, I was at the base. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After you returned to the base, to that school building, you were informed that it was necessary to send your unit to the road from Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje, and in response to a question by the Prosecutor, you said today that that was what you had done. However, I'm interested in particular days. You said that not all of the members of your unit went to secure the road. Can you give us some numbers, how many left, how many stayed?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you numbers, but one part of the unit that was resting -- that had been resting, while the others were in Potocari, they went. And also another group of men that had no other job to do but just stand by the civilians, they were also sent, but I cannot give you the number, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I'm not going to insist. But, at any rate, only a part of your unit went?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, not the full unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood correctly the assignment that you had, and of course I refer to your statement given to the OTP, lines 5 to 10 on page 4, your task was to secure this section of the road so that groups that could be in the area around Bratunac could not enter the town?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, your task was to prevent them from coming into town?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to make it clearer to the Trial Chamber, where exactly your unit was deployed, what kind of deployment it was, how long they stretched, I would like to look at a map, and I will try to help you mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have 4D101 in the court system. Maybe I should repeat the number. It's 4D101. It's going to take some time. It's a voluminous file. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, if I can be of assistance, do you think we should enlarge it, zoom in a bit more?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I cannot see anything here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you zoom it just a bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you see on the map where Bratunac is marked?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you see the road going from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje going to the left from our viewpoint. Can you mark here where you started deploying your men from Bratunac and mark the line along which they were deployed?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, they were deployed up to the -- from the last houses on the periphery of Bratunac. How to mark it here, if this is the centre, then the initial point would be outside of the town. [Marks] And then it went in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we could just see enlarged the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Once the document is marked, we cannot move it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ignore it, however, no? You can ignore it and we can have another one brought -- no, you don't need to save it, you can just ignore it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think we don't need to save it. Just I wanted to show where Glogova is, and it can be seen on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't we do something? Why don't I suggest something different? Madam Usher can perhaps assist the witness to delete that mark, those marks that he's made. Okay? Then we can zoom in the area, perhaps even a little bit more, I don't know, and now it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The left side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, it's the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And left and then in the upper corner, and then the upper corner of this map shows where Glogova is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You need to move it down a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You can even move it towards the right. Yes, and now the witness should be in a better position to mark where Glogova is. Thank you, Madam Registrar, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, in order to indicate exactly approximately, we all know where Bratunac is and where the houses begin from, but in order to mark Glogova, where it is, in order to have an approximate idea of where the members of your unit were deployed along the road on the 12th, the 12th at night?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th at night, my unit was not deployed in Glogova, but it was deployed just up to Glogova. At this map, though, I don't know. If Glogova is here, then it should be somewhere before Glogova. Exactly where this before is, I don't really -- I know this part of Glogova, but I know it from a different aspect, from the positions in Kravica. So like this, it would be difficult for me to give you a precise answer that it was up to here or -- there's no particular marking or bridge or something that I can recognise and then tell you that. Like this on the map, it's difficult. I know that we didn't go into that part of Glogova because I would recognise it. It was up to Glogova, but exactly where that is on this map, I really don't know. If it's -- well, it's very difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then we will not insist if you are not in a position to do that. But in any case, it is your testimony that you didn't go into Glogova, but that you deployed the last member of your unit just up before Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And on the 13th, it was in Glogova, because that was that area that I could recognise from before. So I know that we reached those points, but it was only on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you now, you were earlier in that area, as you explained?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How far is that from the place where the last member of your unit was deployed to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot give an estimate. I'm unable to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then I won't insist. During that night - we're still talking about the night of the 12th - you said you toured your men who were deployed by the road. Did any of them tell you that there had been a conflict or a skirmish? Did any of the members of your unit get involved in the conflict with members of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no skirmishes. You could see on the faces of my men that they were afraid, because they said you could hear somebody was moving in the forest, there was somebody around, but they did not report to me any action, any combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, if something had happened, they would have certainly told you?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they couldn't have concealed it from me. I could have read their faces easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I can just try to clarify the whole situation, you said that only a part of your unit was deployed there, and regardless of the fact that you were unable to mark this map, we are still talking about a stretch of several kilometres. How exactly did you deploy them along the road? What was the criterion? How would you decide where you would put one man or a group of men, how many were needed in each spot, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Jevic told me to do that, he told me that during the night, since there was a shortage of policemen, we would do that so that there would be no incursions into Bratunac, so I placed one or two men at certain intervals, depending on the terrain, so that they have a vantage point in a perimeter, preferably wide. But, frankly, all this has become very vague in my memory. There was no special criterion. I just deployed them at certain intervals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So if I said roughly that perhaps 50 of your men were deployed along a line of several kilometres, that would be a rough idea of how your forces were placed along that road?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move to the 13th of July. On the 13th, in the morning, together with a part of your unit that was not deployed on the road, you returned to Potocari; correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood that correctly, those who were there on the road in the night of the 12th, they stayed behind at the base, and those who had spent the night at the base, they went to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot give you exact numbers. I can say -- I cannot say that 27 went and the others stayed. I can only tell you that it was a smaller group than the day before because we expected a smaller workload.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And at the moment when -- on the 13th, when you arrived in Potocari with a part of your unit, evacuation had been underway for quite a while?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on the 13th, before you arrived, the evacuation was handled only by the Dutchmen?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found them in the same place where I left on the previous day, so I suppose it was handled by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in the course of the 13th, when you and your unit returned to Potocari, you just joined the Dutchmen in what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was just like the day before, although there were no crowds anymore, so it was not necessary to make any cordons like the day before. We were there just to secure the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that day, sometime until 3.00 p.m. -- by 3.00 p.m. your job in Potocari was over?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the last civilians left, we stood by the entrance to the UN base, waiting for our vehicles, and I saw some men I recognised from humanitarian organisations, some men I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your testimony correctly, in fact the statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, on that day you were in contact with Mr. Borovcanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since that was not discussed during your examination-in-chief, could you tell us about the circumstances under which you got into contact with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, when I deployed my men around the civilians, since a number of the civilians was close to the transport organisation, whatever it was called, one of my soldiers informed me that there was a new bus he found in the hangar. I asked whether he could start it, whether it was in working order. He said, "Yes, I'll try." And I said, "Very well. If you manage to start it, then drive it to the base where we are staying." I called up Jevic and I found out from Jevic that Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin insisted that the bus be returned to Bratunac Municipality and that the bus should be theirs. And I must say I didn't quite agree with that because the bus would have been very useful to the Special Brigade because we were on the move very often and we really did not have a surplus of equipment. So the bus was returned, and on the 13th we met up and we discussed it, and I suppose that Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin wanted to let me know that it was only fair towards Bratunac Municipality and they, in their turn, would do us a favour if we needed transportation or something, and that's what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have cleared up that episode. It's certainly useful to know the reason.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one thing remains less than clear. Mr. Borovcanin called you up, not Mr. Dusko Jevic?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I let Jevic know about this whole thing, and Jevic told me what needed to be done. But Mr. Borovcanin probably, as a gentleman, wanted to tell me personally, because it did not concern directly our work. I suppose that's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it's possible also that Mr. Borovcanin was unable to reach Dusko Jevic?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But at any rate, that is the only contact you had with Borovcanin that day?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question about your duties at the time. In addition to that explanation concerning the bus, et cetera, did he maybe give you any orders, instructions, or anything?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any orders or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are still back on the 13th of July. You are still in Potocari that day. You didn't see the 2nd Detachment from Sekovici or the 1st Company of the PJP from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It seems that we don't have your answer on the record. Did you see them or didn't you see them? Tell us again.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is whether -- and Mr. Lazarevic is still keeping you on the 13th of July, whether you are still in Potocari on that day and whether you saw the 2nd Detachment from Sekovici or the 1st Company of the PJP from Zvornik. Let's take them one by one. You confirm that you were still in Potocari on the 13th [Realtime transcript read in error "12th"] of July. That you have confirmed on several occasions. On that day, did you see the 2nd Detachment from Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see the other detachment from Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you see the 1st Company of the PJP from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 1st Company from Zvornik, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have your answer now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one small correction for the transcript. I mean, it is on line 17, page 75, it says "on the 12th of July." "You confirm that you were still in Potocari on the 12th," and it should be "on the 13th."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that day on the 13th in Potocari, did you see any mistreatment, harassment, the seizure of personal property from the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were there, especially on the 13th, in Potocari when the civilians were already evacuated from Potocari, did you see in that entire area a large quantity of discarded personal items, backpacks, items of clothing and other items that the civilian population discarded on their departure because it would have been an additional burden, they didn't know what to do with it?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the place where they were, after they left, a large amount of clothing, footwear, bundles, did remain. We didn't look in the bundles to see what was in them, but in any case a large quantity of articles was left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And these articles were in this broader area where they were put up, these refugees?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony here, we saw some video footage before. This was shown to you by Mr. Thayer, where you recognised yourself, Lieutenant van Duijn, and this young man, Miki?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at that again in order to clarify who is saying what to whom and what it's all about. Can you please carefully look and see what you say to Miki, what Miki says to you, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm afraid I'm not receiving any sound, so I believe that the witness needs to hear it because it's in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your question is quite clear that we need to, but maybe it's a question of we have to wait a little bit or is it a more radical technical problem? Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think past experience has shown that sometimes it takes a little while for the sound to kick in. Maybe if we try again or let it play, it might kick in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I asked it's just a question of time. Sometimes we have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to now hear the sound as well as look at the image?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you heard very clearly your own words directed at Miki, who was interpreting, where you say, "Let them see if they want to go. It's their job"?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, in order to clarify this totally, because you are the one who is saying that and we don't have a better witness who would be able to tell us what was meant by that, therefore, "Let them see if they want to go," who is supposed to see if they want to go?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you say, "if they want to go," who are you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The remaining civilians who were still there in small numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the last part of this sentence, "it's their job," who does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the members of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So from your answers, then, it was the job of the members of the United Nations to go to the Muslim civilians to ask them if they wanted to go or if they wanted to stay, and then to inform you about it, and then those who wanted to go can proceed to the buses?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, it was our job only to secure that, just security, no movement of civilians or any other organisation of transport or anything related to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, that is how I understood your role as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just to cut one redirect question while we're on the topic, if we could just find out when the witness's recollection is that this particular clip occurred on the 13th, just so we have a time frame established for this exchange. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, I think you can address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means. I mean, I believe that both my colleague and myself, we both know when this footage was shot, but I will ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what you can recall, when was this filmed, on the 12th, on the 13th, what time?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the time. I cannot give you the exact time because I did not observe events according to a clock or a watch. I know that this was close to the place that I indicated on the map where we were the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this satisfy my colleague's inquiry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He doesn't know the time. I mean, Mr. Thayer has to be satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As for the participation of the DutchBat in the evacuation of the civilians from Potocari, would you agree with my assertion that their role in the organisation of the evacuation was an active one?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, pertaining to the evacuation, I would just like to discuss one detail. We heard here a certain number of testimonies that, in the UN base itself, in the fenced-in area of the base, there were over 4.000 civilians. Can you, as somebody who was there, who was nearby, tell us, these civilians who were in the base itself, how were they evacuated? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't enter the UN base. I don't know how many civilians were there or what was there. I know that there were some people there, and I recall Dusko telling me that these were the civilians who arrived on the night before the 12th or in the night of the 12th. But in any case, they stayed in the UN base, and these who were arriving on the 12th didn't go in the base itself, but they stayed outside with all the others. I really don't know how these people who are in the base itself were transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What I'm mostly interested in, in relation to this, is whether you, yourself, or the people from your unit had any kind of contact or had anything to do with the evacuation of the civilians that were in the base itself.

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th and the 13th of July, did you ever enter the UN base in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said that I never entered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just a couple of questions and then we will be finished for today. You don't speak English, do you?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All your communication with members of the Dutch Battalion was conducted with the assistance of a member of your unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This member of your unit who was interpreting for you and the Dutch side was not a professional interpreter, was he?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. As far as I know, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And since you didn't speak English, cannot say how much the interpretation of the communication between you and the Dutch Battalion was correct?

utterances.speaker: MENDELJEV DJURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to move to another topic, and I have just one more minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfectly fine with us. Mr. Djuric, we'll finish here today. We'll stop here. We'll continue tomorrow morning, and hopefully we will finish with your testimony tomorrow. May I also remind you of what I told you yesterday, that you're not to communicate with anyone or allow anyone to communicate with you to discuss the subject matter of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have a nice afternoon, all of you, and we'll meet again tomorrow morning.
